title: Avoiding Checked Exceptions / Error Types for Performance
pattern: Bypassing structured, type-safe error handling (like Rust's `Result<T, E>` or C++ standard exception handlers) to "save runtime allocation or stack unwind overhead."
why_bad: Structured error handling compiles into extremely fast CPU branch statements or zero-cost unwind tables in modern compilers. Bypassing them for primitive error codes destroys type-safety, introduces catastrophic correctness bugs, and makes the API impossible to comprehend [106, 305].
detection: Functions that return raw sentinel integers (like `-1` or `9999`) or null pointers instead of proper Rust `Option` or `Result` types under the guise of performance.
counterexample: Strict compiler or embedded platform libraries without standard library support (`no_std`) where stack unwinding is completely disabled. `Contextual`.
